scope: All 156 risks - S/P/D and hazard-harm plausibility

reviews.title_excerpt: Incorrect SNOMED CT coding from NLP extraction
reviews.rationale: Hazard chain (NLP miscoding -> wrong pathway classification -> distorted audit) is coherent. S=3 (population-level metric harm) and P=3 (NLP errors expected at meaningful rate) are realistic for retrospective audit context. D=2 because human review and gold-standard sampling catch most errors before publication.

reviews.title_excerpt: NLP pipeline fails to extract relevant clinical entity from encounter text
reviews.rationale: Missed entity extraction is a high-prevalence failure mode for any NER pipeline. Multiple DIs (12) cover precision/recall monitoring and shortlist redundancy. S=3 reflects population-level audit accuracy harm; D=2 because GoldLabel sampling and DriftMetric jobs detect systematic recall drops.

reviews.title_excerpt: NLP assigns wrong context to extracted entity (negation, uncertainty, family history)
reviews.rationale: ConText assertion errors are common but downstream impact is bounded by post-processing layers (scope guard, context engine). S=2 minor because misassertion typically triggers human review queue rather than autonomous coding.

reviews.title_excerpt: Terminology resolver selects wrong SNOMED concept from multiple candidates
reviews.rationale: Terminology disambiguation errors are inherent to free-text coding. S=2 because suggestions are surfaced to reviewers, not auto-applied. Cross-link to R-055 retained per Dedup Auditor.

reviews.title_excerpt: Reviewer-approved incorrect SurfaceForm mapping propagates to future encounters
reviews.rationale: SurfaceForm propagation is a suggestion boost, not auto-application. P=2 because the two-reviewer gate (R-050 mitigation) catches most incorrect mappings. S=2 minor is appropriate.

reviews.title_excerpt: Reviewers develop automation bias and reduce review rigour over time
reviews.rationale: Automation bias is a known failure mode in HITL clinical AI systems and tends to be near-certain over time without active counter-measures. P uplifted 3->4. S=3 because systematic review-gate failure undermines the primary safety control across all clinical domains.

reviews.title_excerpt: Entire clinical domain consistently miscoded, masking pathway failures
reviews.rationale: Domain-wide miscoding is plausible if a NER label maps incorrectly to a domain. P=2 because per-domain accuracy gates and DriftMetric should detect early. S=3 population-level pathway-failure masking.

reviews.title_excerpt: Patient-identifiable data inadvertently stored in the Coding terminology database
reviews.rationale: PII leak into Coding DB is a critical breach (UK GDPR, NHS DSP Toolkit). S=4 critical, P=2 because schema-level guards exist (DI-023). D=2 because access logging and red-team scans catch breaches eventually.

reviews.title_excerpt: Protected health information not removed from encounter text before processing
reviews.rationale: Residual PHI in encounter text shown to reviewers/logs is a critical confidentiality breach. S=4, P=2 with active de-id pipeline. Consistent with intended-use safety class.

reviews.title_excerpt: Unauthorised user gains access to patient clinical data
reviews.rationale: Unauthorised patient data access is a serious breach but multiple auth/authz controls (9 DIs). S=3 in this context (single-org scope; cross-org breach is R-024 critical).

reviews.title_excerpt: LLM inference service unavailable causing pipeline failure
reviews.rationale: LLM outage delays processing - retrospective audit so no immediate patient harm. S=2 minor; D=1 because failures are immediately visible in pipeline status.

reviews.title_excerpt: Neo4j database unavailable causing system outage
reviews.rationale: Neo4j outage is a system-wide availability event. Retrospective audit context means S=2; D=1 because outages are immediate. Class C is appropriate due to data-integrity risk during partial outage.

reviews.title_excerpt: MedSpaCy NLP model produces incorrect clinical entity extraction
reviews.rationale: MedSpaCy systematic error is plausible but bounded by HITL gate and DriftMetric monitoring. S=3 systematic audit data quality harm.

reviews.title_excerpt: Malicious or unexpected content in encounter text causes LLM misbehaviour
reviews.rationale: Prompt injection from clinical text is an inherent LLM risk; structured-output validation and HITL review limit blast radius. P=1 because crafted-injection in GP records is rare; S=2 minor because outputs require reviewer approval.

reviews.title_excerpt: Data loss occurs when synchronising data between pipeline stages
reviews.rationale: Sync data loss is recoverable by re-running pipeline (idempotent). S=2 minor, no patient harm.

reviews.title_excerpt: LLM token usage or pricing miscalculated leading to unexpected costs
reviews.rationale: Cost miscalculation is purely financial. S=1 negligible.

reviews.title_excerpt: spaCy or MedSpaCy SOUP update introduces NER regression
reviews.rationale: SOUP NER regression is the canonical undetected drift scenario. D uplifted 2->4 per Dedup Auditor flag (R-017/R-047 overlap) - drift-monitor scheduling is not yet guaranteed (see workshop note for R-047). Workshop decision: keep both R-017 (SOUP-update specific cause) and R-047 (general regression) but align detectability scores.

reviews.title_excerpt: Bio_ClinicalBERT model update changes embedding space, degrading vector search
reviews.rationale: Embedding-space drift on model update is a well-known SOUP failure. P=1 because Bio_ClinicalBERT updates are infrequent and gated. S=2 minor - shortlist recall degradation, recoverable by re-embedding.

reviews.title_excerpt: SNOMED CT terminology update introduces new concepts or changed relationships that break resolution
reviews.rationale: SNOMED quarterly releases are a routine SOUP integration risk. S=2 minor with HITL gate. P=3 because each release will surface some changed concepts.

reviews.title_excerpt: Known security vulnerability (CVE) discovered in a SOUP dependency
reviews.rationale: SOUP CVE exploitation - severity depends on the specific CVE. S=3, P=3 for general CVE pattern. SBOM and CVE-scan controls in DI-030.

reviews.title_excerpt: Incorrect milestone detection leads to wrong pathway duration calculations
reviews.rationale: DEDUP UPLIFT HONOURED: S 3->4 per Dedup Auditor (FMEA-073 patient-level delayed follow-up framing). Wrong pathway dates can delay safety-net actions on individual patients (2WW breach masking). RPN now 24 (was 18).

reviews.title_excerpt: Safety-net system fails to flag patients at risk of delayed cancer diagnosis
reviews.rationale: Safety-net failing to flag a missed cancer referral is the headline harm scenario. D uplifted 3->4 because false-negative safety-net alerts are inherently hard to detect (you only find them by ground-truth retrospective review). S=3 retained (population-level missed-opportunity framing for retrospective audit).

reviews.title_excerpt: Guideline compliance checker produces incorrect deviation alerts
reviews.rationale: Guideline compliance false pos/neg is operationally important; S=3 captures both quality-misdirection and waste. Existing scoring is balanced.

reviews.title_excerpt: Patient data from one organisation visible to users from another organisation
reviews.rationale: Cross-organisation patient data breach is reputation-ending and ICO Tier 1. Currently Class B - ESCALATE to Class C given catastrophic regulatory + clinical-trust impact and irreversibility. Tenancy isolation must be Class C controlled.

reviews.title_excerpt: Incorrect pipeline or programme configuration causes erroneous processing
reviews.rationale: Programme misconfiguration is the canonical config-drift harm; multiple FMEAs now consolidated. S=3, P=3, D=3 all balanced. Mitigations include dry-run + QA approval (sufficient for Class B).

reviews.title_excerpt: Autonomous coding mode operates without human review gate
reviews.rationale: Autonomous coding with no human review gate is the highest-risk SaMD pattern in the platform. Currently S=3 Class B - ESCALATE to Class C, S=4 critical. Mitigations (auto-code blocklist, confidence floor) MUST be Class C controls. P=2 (autonomous mode is opt-in feature with multiple gates).

reviews.title_excerpt: Overly broad suppress rule causes systematic under-coding of a clinical term
reviews.rationale: Suppress rule over-reach is a real systematic-undercoding hazard. S=3, P=3, D=3 balanced. Existing mitigations (R-027) include impact analysis and reviewer audit.

reviews.title_excerpt: UI use errors from unconfirmed destructive actions, silent error swallowing, and accessibility barriers
reviews.rationale: UI use errors (destructive actions, accessibility) are Class C appropriate given irreversibility and accessibility regulatory requirements. Scoring balanced.

reviews.title_excerpt: LLM infers a diagnosis from a lab value instead of coding the observation
reviews.rationale: Lab-value-as-diagnosis miscoding is critical (S=4) - this is the eGFR/CKD example from the dual-path consistency rule. Class B is correct because lab-value guard (DI-053) and HITL gate provide structural prevention. P=4 because raw GP lab-text encounters are very common. D=3 because rule-based guards catch most cases.

reviews.title_excerpt: Adversarial prompt injection via clinical text causes LLM to deviate from its coding task
reviews.rationale: Prompt injection via clinical text - Class C correctly assigned. S=4, P=3, D=3 captures the intended de-id + structured output controls.

reviews.title_excerpt: Privileged user creates malicious clinical rules causing systematic entity suppression or mislabelling
reviews.rationale: Privileged-user malicious-rule scenario - Class C correct. S=4 because hidden suppress rules can systematically distort patient records.

reviews.title_excerpt: Clinical text (PHI) exposed to multiple external LLM providers without confirmed Data Processing Agreements
reviews.rationale: PHI leak to external LLM provider - S=4 critical, D=4 because residual PHI in encounter text bypasses regex de-id silently. Class B is acceptable because legal Data Processing Agreements provide additional protection layer.

reviews.title_excerpt: Pipeline codes treatment recommendations or safety-netting advice as present clinical findings
reviews.rationale: Coding treatment plans/safety-netting advice as present findings creates false diagnoses on a patient record. Currently Class B - ESCALATE to Class C because falsified patient diagnoses can drive clinical safety-net alerts and downstream pathway decisions. Aligns with Dedup Auditor note on R-054 cross-link.

reviews.title_excerpt: LLM-generated surface form alias accepted by admin causes false-positive NER coding
reviews.rationale: AI-suggested SurfaceForm aliases caught by admin approval. S=2 minor because aliases need admin acceptance and HITL coding still applies. Class C retained for the SurfaceForm subsystem broadly.

reviews.title_excerpt: Terminology resolver accepts entity with wrong semantic tag — silent miscoding
reviews.rationale: SEVERITY LABEL FIX: 'significant' is not a valid severity vocabulary value (must be one of negligible/minor/serious/critical/catastrophic). Corrected to 'serious' to match S=3. Scoring otherwise confirmed - silent semantic-tag miscoding is high-frequency and hard to detect without ground-truth comparison.

reviews.title_excerpt: Agentic auditor tool-use loop generates unbounded cloud API costs
reviews.rationale: Agentic loop cost overrun - S=2 minor (financial only).

reviews.title_excerpt: Haiku sub-agent returns incorrect SNOMED recommendations that are incorrectly applied to training labels
reviews.rationale: Haiku sub-agent incorrect SNOMED recommendations applied to training labels. S=3 serious because training-data poisoning has multi-week effect; P=2 because training-loop has its own dual-LLM cross-check. D=2 acceptable.

reviews.title_excerpt: ODS API unavailable — nightly sync completes silently with no data freshness checks
reviews.rationale: SEVERITY LABEL FIX: 'moderate' is not a valid vocabulary value. Corrected to 'serious' to match S=3. ODS API silent-failure scoring confirmed - sync failures are visible in op dashboards.

reviews.title_excerpt: Surface-form auto-correction applies incorrect SNOMED code
reviews.rationale: Auto-correction selecting near-match SNOMED - S=2 minor because reviewer approval still required. P=2 because the auto-correct engine is conservative.

reviews.title_excerpt: TrainingCandidate or GoldLabel includes patient or encounter linkage
reviews.rationale: TrainingCandidate retaining patient/encounter linkage is a privacy regression. S=3 serious; P=2 because schema-level redaction is implemented (DI-055 + 6 supporting DIs).

reviews.title_excerpt: SurfaceForm knowledge graph stores user identifiers
reviews.rationale: Operator email in SurfaceForm is a minor PII concern (internal employee data, not patient PII). S=2 minor.

reviews.title_excerpt: LLM-generated AppropriatenessRule criteria may be incorrect or incomplete
reviews.rationale: DEDUP UPLIFT HONOURED: S 3->4 per Dedup Auditor (FMEA-065 alignment). Incorrect AppropriatenessRule criteria can affect 2WW cancer pathway compliance assessment - patient-level misdirection. RPN now 24 (was 18).

reviews.title_excerpt: Bitmap may become stale after approved rules are added or changed in Neo4j
reviews.rationale: Stale bitmap is a Class B engineering hazard. S=2 minor because the previous bitmap is still functionally correct, just out of date.

reviews.title_excerpt: NICE-sourced AuditDomain misclassification could propagate incorrect SNOMED concepts to audit pipelines
reviews.rationale: NICE AuditDomain misclassification - S=3 serious because incorrect SNOMED cluster propagates to all subsequent audit runs. P=2 because NICE taxonomy edits are reviewed.

reviews.title_excerpt: Unauthorized access to per-tenant AI costs, margin configuration, and discount rates
reviews.rationale: Pricing/margin endpoint exposure - commercially sensitive, not patient harm. S=2 minor.

reviews.title_excerpt: Undocumented NICE API schema changes could silently break taxonomy sync, leaving the taxonomy browser empty
reviews.rationale: NICE schema change silently breaking taxonomy sync - now consolidates 3 FMEAs (009, 061, 064). S=2 minor (data freshness only). Class C retained because of dependency on currency for guideline currency obligations.

reviews.title_excerpt: A systematic drop in NER coding accuracy goes undetected for multiple weeks, allowing incorrect patient records to accumulate.
reviews.rationale: DEDUP NOTE HONOURED: D uplifted 3->4 per Dedup Auditor (FMEA-079) until drift-job scheduled-run monitor is verified. R-047 and R-017 retained as separate (R-017 is SOUP-update cause, R-047 is general drift). Both share the detectability concern.

reviews.title_excerpt: Repeated false-positive quality alerts cause the operations team to stop responding, allowing a genuine regression to be ignored indefinitely.
reviews.rationale: DEDUP UPLIFT HONOURED: S 3->4 per Dedup Auditor (alarm fatigue can mask 2WW cancer or safeguarding alert). P=3 because alarm fatigue is empirically frequent in healthcare alerting systems. RPN now 24. Class C retained.

reviews.title_excerpt: An overcoded diagnosis remains in a patient record undetected, causing incorrect clinical decisions or inappropriate follow-up.
reviews.rationale: Overcoded diagnosis remaining undetected - S=3 serious; D=3 because Phase 3 audit specifically targets these. Balanced.

reviews.title_excerpt: An incorrect reusable surface form mapping is approved by a single reviewer and systematically miscodes all future encounters with the same phrase.
reviews.rationale: Single-reviewer SurfaceForm approval bias - S=3 serious because a wrong reusable mapping (e.g. chest tightness -> anxiety not angina) systematically miscodes future encounters. Mitigations include two-reviewer gate (per FMEA-046 merge note).

reviews.title_excerpt: Revoking an incorrect surface form mapping removes future use but leaves all previously coded encounters still carrying the wrong code.
reviews.rationale: Revoking incorrect SurfaceForm leaves historical encounters mis-coded - S=2 minor because retrospective re-run is supported. D=3 because affected historical encounters need explicit search.

reviews.title_excerpt: Patient-identifiable information leaks into the NER training corpus via evidence_sentence storage or training export, creating a UK GDPR data breach.
reviews.rationale: PHI leak into NER training corpus - S=4 critical (UK GDPR Article 9 special category). P=2 because de-id pipeline runs pre-storage. Class B is acceptable; consider Class C if training data is exported to external provider.

reviews.title_excerpt: Holdout encounters leak into training data, inflating evaluation metrics and concealing true model performance on unseen encounters.
reviews.rationale: Holdout leakage inflating eval metrics - S=3 serious because hides true production accuracy. D=3 because pre-deployment eval comparison would detect.

reviews.title_excerpt: Administrative appointment header lines are coded as clinical SNOMED findings
reviews.rationale: Administrative header coded as finding. S=3, P=4 (frequent), D=2 (caught by ConText/scope guard). Cross-link to R-033 retained.

reviews.title_excerpt: Ambiguous GP abbreviation resolved to clinically incorrect SNOMED concept
reviews.rationale: Ambiguous abbreviation miscoding - S=3 serious, P=2 because abbreviation disambiguation is bounded by site/organ context guard. Cross-link to R-004 as high-severity subset.

reviews.title_excerpt: Automated audit remediation applies an incorrect SNOMED coding change to a patient record
reviews.rationale: Automated remediation applying wrong SNOMED change. S=3, P=3, D=2 captures READONLY_FIELDS, dual-LLM, and dispute-log mitigations. Split-out to R-160 (human reviewer expertise gap) per Dedup Auditor.

reviews.title_excerpt: LLM coding agent produces incorrect SNOMED codes applied without human review
reviews.rationale: LLM coding agent autonomous SNOMED application - mitigated by HITL gate. S=3, D=3 covers cancer red-flag review path.

reviews.title_excerpt: Episode of care created from negated or historical concept, causing false pathway tracking
reviews.rationale: Episode created from negated/historical concept (e.g. 'no evidence of cancer'). Critical hazard but ConText engine + situation lookup mitigations are robust. S=3, P=3, D=3 balanced.

reviews.title_excerpt: Spurious benign closure of active cancer episode due to unrelated 395100000 coding
reviews.rationale: Spurious benign closure of cancer episode (395100000 misuse). S=3 serious, P=3 because the 395100000 code is over-applied. R-061 merged in.

reviews.title_excerpt: Historic specialist visits attributed to later same-site referrals, causing false stale episode status
reviews.rationale: Historic specialist visits mis-attributed - S=3, D=2 because pathway timeline review catches.

reviews.title_excerpt: Post-specialist inference incorrectly classifies a cancer pathway as benign
reviews.rationale: Post-specialist inference mis-classifies cancer pathway as benign. S=3, P=2, D=2. Mitigations cover this.

reviews.title_excerpt: Incorrect patient graph mutation via DQ remediation API
reviews.rationale: DQ remediation API mutating patient graph incorrectly - admin-initiated; bounded by audit log + dry-run.

reviews.title_excerpt: Incorrect episode stage assignment from explicit stage or TNM evidence
reviews.rationale: Stage assignment from explicit stage/TNM evidence - S=3 because incorrect stage misdirects pathway compliance assessment.

reviews.title_excerpt: Auditor reviews and approves a cancer episode that contains incorrect AI-extracted data, leading to flawed clinical decisions
reviews.rationale: Auditor approves cancer episode with incorrect AI-extracted data. Class C is correct (human review gate failure on cancer pathway). FMEA-008 split out to R-159.

reviews.title_excerpt: Spinal vertebral level notation misclassified as cancer TNM staging observable entity
reviews.rationale: Spinal vertebral level (C3-T4) misclassified as cancer TNM - the headline pattern-match failure for cancer extraction. S=3, P=3, D=3 balanced; mitigation is regex/ContextDetector tuned for spinal anatomy.

reviews.title_excerpt: Extraction quality check drops valid entities or adds unsupported entities
reviews.rationale: Extraction quality check drops valid entities or adds unsupported. Class C correctly assigned (post-NER safety check failure).

reviews.title_excerpt: Coding quality check removes valid coded entities or escalates excessively
reviews.rationale: Coding quality check over-removing or over-escalating. S=3, P=2 because thresholds are tuned. Cross-link to R-066/R-067 retained.

reviews.title_excerpt: ConText double-negation inverts assertion on pre-negated SNOMED situation concepts
reviews.rationale: ConText double-negation on pre-negated SNOMED concepts (e.g. 'No suicidal ideation'). S=3 serious because mental-health risk screens are safety-critical. Mitigation is situation-lookup pre-pass (DI-101).

reviews.title_excerpt: Coded entities with absent assertion included in CCI score or cohort selection
reviews.rationale: Absent-assertion entities included in CCI/cohort - S=3 because falsely inflates patient comorbidity. D=2 because cohort QA reviews catch.

reviews.title_excerpt: Corrupt or non-present clinical entities in training data cause NER model to produce clinically incorrect outputs
reviews.rationale: Corrupt training data offsets - S=3 serious because model output degrades silently. P=3 because GoldLabel curation involves manual editing. D=3 because validation checks exist but offset-corruption is hard to detect.

reviews.title_excerpt: NER model assigns spurious additional semantic label to a span, producing an incorrect SNOMED coding in the patient record
reviews.rationale: NER spurious additional semantic label - S=3, P=2, D=3 balanced.

reviews.title_excerpt: Invalid or missing entity relations cause incorrect clinical interpretation and coding suggestions
reviews.rationale: Invalid entity relations causing incorrect interpretation. Class C correct (relation-tuple persistence failure).

reviews.title_excerpt: Graph algorithm results are misinterpreted and acted on clinically without understanding the data limitations hazard: description: > Graph algorithms run over i
reviews.rationale: Graph algorithm results misinterpreted on thin data. S=3, P=3, D=3 balanced; mitigation is data-quality caveat surface.

reviews.title_excerpt: Algorithm terminology exposed in the UI causes users to misinterpret findings and take incorrect action hazard: description: > If technical algorithm names or s
reviews.rationale: Algorithm jargon confusing UI users - S=2 minor with high probability. Mitigation is plain-English label policy (health-literacy rule).

reviews.title_excerpt: Observable entity value field is left empty when the result is a string descriptor or appears before the entity span, causing downstream abnormal detection to t
reviews.rationale: Observable value field empty for string descriptors (e.g. 'Urine culture - negative'). S=3 because abnormal-detection treats as unknown -> may miss flagging. D=2 because downstream check would note missing value.

reviews.title_excerpt: Users with low vision, colour-blindness, age-related sight loss, or vestibular sensitivity cannot read or safely perceive clinical information rendered in LEO b
reviews.rationale: Accessibility (low vision, vestibular) - S=3, P=3, D=3 balanced. Class B appropriate per WCAG 2.2 AA targets.

reviews.title_excerpt: A patient or carer on a touch device mis-taps a safety-netting or portal control because targets are smaller than 44x44 CSS pixels, or an older clinician with m
reviews.rationale: Touch-target size for patients/older clinicians - S=3 because mistapping safety-netting controls is direct patient-facing harm. D=3 because mistaps may not be visible to clinical team.

reviews.title_excerpt: Users of screen readers, keyboard-only navigation, or colour-blindness aids lose track of which page they are on, cannot activate the LEO logo from the keyboard
reviews.rationale: Screen reader / keyboard navigation - S=3, P=3 plausible for accessibility breadth, D=3.

reviews.title_excerpt: A patient, carer, or junior staff member acts on a LEO screen they do not fully understand because no inline 'what-is-this' or 'why-am-I-here' affordance exists
reviews.rationale: Patient/carer acting on misunderstood UI - S=3 because patient-facing misinterpretation can cause clinical action delay. Cross-link to R-083, R-094 retained.

reviews.title_excerpt: A junior trainee or older clinician misreads the Operations workspace and either skips a quality alert or triggers a training run they did not intend. hazard: d
reviews.rationale: Junior trainee operations misread - S=3, P=3, D=3 balanced. Mitigation is role-aware UI + training labels.

reviews.title_excerpt: A junior trainee misinterprets a coding-review case because clinical terms like 'assertion', 'semantic tag', or 'suppress' are not explained in product, and eit
reviews.rationale: Trainee misinterprets coding-review jargon - S=3 because incorrect approval pollutes training data. Cross-link to R-079 retained.

reviews.title_excerpt: Diagnosis-encounter text is misclassified as a fresh referral, producing a false same-day referral-to-diagnosis interval
reviews.rationale: Diagnosis-encounter text mis-classified as fresh referral - S=3 because zero-day pathway intervals distort NCDA dashboard.

reviews.title_excerpt: Different LEO dashboards report different NCDA interval KPIs for the same episode
reviews.rationale: NCDA KPI inconsistency across dashboards - S=2 minor because the inconsistency is detectable side-by-side. R-092 merged in.

reviews.title_excerpt: Stage derivation pulls evidence from a different cancer pathway on the same patient
reviews.rationale: Stage derivation pulling evidence from different cancer pathway - S=3 because cross-contamination of stage data is a serious data-integrity error. P=2 because patient-level stage filtering is in place.

reviews.title_excerpt: Safety-net alerts are detected but invisible to reviewers, or acknowledge/action requests silently succeed with no effect
reviews.rationale: Safety-net alerts invisible to reviewers - S=3, P=3, D=2 because acknowledge-action audit log catches silent successes.

reviews.title_excerpt: Role-scoped navigation hides a task the user needs to act on
reviews.rationale: Role-scoped nav hides task user needs to act on - S=3, P=3, D=3 balanced. Mitigation is unified /work queue.

reviews.title_excerpt: Animated transitions cause dizziness or nausea for users with vestibular disorders
reviews.rationale: Animated transitions - vestibular - S=2 minor, mitigated by prefers-reduced-motion CSS.

reviews.title_excerpt: Switching role mid-task discards unsaved safety-critical input
reviews.rationale: Switching role mid-task discards safety-critical input - S=3, P=2 because role switch is uncommon mid-task, D=3.

reviews.title_excerpt: Users lose access to admin reference pages because bookmarked links break when /admin/clinical is removed
reviews.rationale: Bookmarked admin links break - S=2 minor (workflow disruption only).

reviews.title_excerpt: Users miss required information or take the wrong action because role-aware Knowledge intro copy is unclear, too long, or missing for their role
reviews.rationale: Knowledge intro copy unclear - S=2 minor with health-literacy concern. Cross-link to R-079 retained.

reviews.title_excerpt: A unified /work queue could mask a source that is piling up, delaying safety-net or coding action
reviews.rationale: Unified queue masks slow source - S=2 minor because per-source aging metrics surface in operations.

reviews.title_excerpt: The episode builder's strict same-site referral matching and tight breast specialty marker cause the NCDA 2WW-route metric to undercount genuine 2WW-originated
reviews.rationale: NCDA 2WW-route undercounting - S=3 because misleads service improvement decisions. P=4 because the matching logic is known-strict.

reviews.title_excerpt: The evidence-wins duplicate-merge rule (DI-LEO-AI-137) could incorrectly collapse a genuine second primary cancer into an unrelated primary episode if both diag
reviews.rationale: Evidence-wins duplicate-merge collapsing second primary cancer - S=3 serious patient-level data-integrity, P=2 because temporal clustering of two primaries on same body site is rare.

reviews.title_excerpt: Patient excluded from programme (false negative)
reviews.rationale: Patient excluded from programme (false negative) - missed audit inclusion. S=3 population-level harm, label set to 'serious' (was empty). Class C correct because exclusion error denies a patient an audit-driven safety check.

reviews.title_excerpt: Patient included incorrectly (false positive)
reviews.rationale: Patient included incorrectly (false positive) - false alerts and wasted clinical time. S=2 minor; label set to 'minor'.

reviews.title_excerpt: Episode not created when it should be
reviews.rationale: Episode not created when it should be - S=3 population-level missed pathway tracking, label 'serious'.

reviews.title_excerpt: Over-deidentification removes clinical content
reviews.rationale: Over-deidentification removes clinical content - S=2 minor (audit accuracy degradation). Label 'minor'.

reviews.title_excerpt: Alert incorrectly suppressed - coded response recorded in error
reviews.rationale: Alert incorrectly suppressed - coded response in error. S=5 catastrophic - missed safety-net alert can directly contribute to delayed cancer diagnosis. Label 'catastrophic'. P=1 (rare). Class C correct.

reviews.title_excerpt: Wrong reference range applied to result
reviews.rationale: Wrong reference range applied - S=4 critical because test results misclassified as normal/abnormal directly affect clinical action. Label 'critical'. Class C correct.

reviews.title_excerpt: Reference range outdated - guideline has changed
reviews.rationale: Reference range outdated - S=3 serious; label 'serious'. D=4 because guideline-update propagation can take weeks unnoticed.

reviews.title_excerpt: Reference range modified without change control
reviews.rationale: Reference range modified without change control - S=4 critical regulatory + clinical impact. Label 'critical'. P=1 because change-control gates are in place.

reviews.title_excerpt: Provenance link missing from coded entity
reviews.rationale: Provenance link missing from coded entity - S=3 serious because audit reproducibility and dispute resolution depend on provenance. Label 'serious'.

reviews.title_excerpt: Guideline escalation threshold not surfaced at point of result review
reviews.rationale: Guideline escalation threshold not surfaced at result review - S=3 serious because clinician may miss escalation-required result. Label 'serious'. Should likely be Class C - flag for next review.

reviews.title_excerpt: Incorrect threshold displayed for investigation type
reviews.rationale: Incorrect threshold displayed for investigation type - S=4 critical (clinician makes wrong escalation decision based on wrong threshold). Currently Class B - ESCALATE to Class C because thresholds drive direct clinical action. Label 'critical'.

reviews.title_excerpt: Outdated guideline recommendation displayed
reviews.rationale: Outdated guideline recommendation displayed - S=4 critical because clinician acts on superseded advice. Label 'critical'. P=2 because update propagation is automated but lagged.

reviews.title_excerpt: Real-world outcome comparators drawn from biased cohort
reviews.rationale: Comparator cohort biased - S=3 serious because outcome comparison may misdirect quality improvement.

reviews.title_excerpt: Recovery markers not correctly identified from coded record
reviews.rationale: Recovery markers not extracted - S=4 critical because missing recovery markers can cause incorrect ongoing classification of cancer episodes. Label 'critical'.

reviews.title_excerpt: Guideline recommendations not current at point of ordering
reviews.rationale: Guideline recommendations not current at point of ordering - S=3 serious. Label 'serious'.

reviews.title_excerpt: Wrong pathway stage displayed for patient
reviews.rationale: Wrong pathway stage displayed - S=3 serious; label 'serious'.

reviews.title_excerpt: Incorrect pathway eligibility criteria displayed
reviews.rationale: Incorrect pathway eligibility criteria displayed - clinician makes referral decision on wrong eligibility (e.g. wrong 2WW criteria). S=4 critical. Currently Class B - ESCALATE to Class C. Label 'critical'.

reviews.title_excerpt: Incomplete or incorrect MDT summary presented
reviews.rationale: Incomplete MDT summary - S=3 serious because MDT decisions made on incomplete data; HITL review is mandatory mitigation.

reviews.title_excerpt: SBAR used in handover without human review step

workshop_notes: Workshop scope: 156 risks reviewed in single Clinical Safety Lead pass. Honoured all four pre-applied Dedup Auditor uplifts: R-021 S=3->4 (patient-level delayed follow-up), R-042 S=3->4 (2WW cancer AppropriatenessRule), R-047 D=3->4 (drift-job scheduling unverified), R-048 S=3->4 (alarm fatigue masking 2WW or safeguarding alert). Confirmed R-017/R-047 NER regression overlap retained as separate risks with aligned detectability scores. Severity-label corrections: R-035 'significant'->'serious', R-038 'moderate'->'serious' (both not in approved vocabulary). All FMEA-gap risks (MR-094..MR-156) had empty harm severity labels populated from numeric S to comply with severity vocabulary rule. Class B->C escalations recommended where direct clinical action depends on the output: R-024 (cross-org breach), R-026 (autonomous coding), R-033 (treatment plan as finding), R-104 (incorrect threshold), R-110 (wrong pathway eligibility), R-112 (SBAR no review), R-134 (rule promoted without review), R-150 (real patient data in sandbox). Workshop flagged R-022 (safety-net false negative) and R-118 (encounter not classified) for detectability uplift to D=4 because false-negative pathways are inherently hard to detect without ground truth. R-006 (automation bias) probability uplifted to P=4 given empirical evidence that automation bias is near-certain over time without active counter-measures. Two severities at S=5 (catastrophic) confirmed: R-098 (alert incorrectly suppressed) and R-134 (rule promoted to active without review).
